RedRock is an unofficial, personal project.

It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by, or approved by Microsoft, Mojang Studios, Xbox, Google, Meta, or any of their subsidiaries.

Minecraft® is a trademark of Mojang Synergies AB / Microsoft. Google Play™ and Android are trademarks of Google LLC. Meta Quest® and Horizon OS are trademarks of Meta Platforms, Inc.

RedRock only downloads apps the signed-in Google account already owns, for personal use on this user’s devices. It does not sell, host, or redistribute APKs. Play may refuse a download. That is not a bypass.

Use at your own risk.

RedRock is a Quest window for Minecraft you already own.\n\nIt is not a store copy and not a cracked APK. This window is the library. Play fills the same window — it does not dump you into stereo VR yet.

Left sidebar is the main chrome.

• Grass block — Game
• Toolbox — native mods
• Books — these docs
• Computer — live log
• Sliders — Settings

The bottom bar holds the Minecraft version picker and Play. Tap the version to choose Latest (Play’s current build) or a specific release. If Minecraft is not on the headset yet, Play says Download.
The Game tab is the grass block. The big cube in the middle is just the hero — Play (or Download) lives on the bottom bar.\n\nPress a tab to lift it toward you. That is how you know it is selected.

Download talks to Google Play as the account that owns Minecraft. Press Play when the button says Download.

1. Use a Google account that already owns the app.
2. Sign in on the page RedRock opens. RedRock never reads your password.
3. Play must allow the download. If it refuses, you do not own it, or Play blocked it.

No mirrors. No paid bypass. Quest needs the arm64 build.

Once Minecraft is on the headset, Play starts it in this same 2D window. It does not install Minecraft as a separate Quest app.\n\nIf the button still says Download, the game is not on disk yet. Stereo OpenXR is later.

In the library window:
• Laser pointer + trigger to click

In the game menu:
• Point + trigger, or A to confirm
• Stick up / down to move the highlight
• B to leave

Look, Volume, and Google account are on the Settings tab.

Settings has two pages: Google and Mixer.

Google shows the signed-in Play profile so you can check it is the right account. Tap the card to sign in. When signed in, Sign out or Switch account.

Look and Volume are local to this window for now. They are not written out to Minecraft yet.

Sideloaded RedRock does not sit in the Store library or the bottom dock.

1. Press the Meta button
2. Open Apps / Library
3. Left side — folder with a question mark — Unknown Sources
4. RedRock

If that folder is missing, toggle Developer Mode off and on in the phone app, then reboot.

The toolbox tab is the mod loader. RedRock Core is always on and loads into the hosted game (mod_preinit, then libminecraftpe, then mod_init). Extra mods are mcpelauncher-style arm64 .so files — not Java Fabric/Forge jars and not marketplace add-ons.

Add a mod
1. Put an arm64-v8a .so on the headset (Files / Downloads, or adb).
2. On the toolbox tab, press Add and pick that .so.
3. Toggle Off to skip it on the next Play, or Remove to delete it.
4. Press Play.

From a computer you can still run:
./redrock mods push libThatMod.so

Quest is arm64-v8a. An x86 or x86_64 mcpelauncher .so from the Mac will not load. Mods that call mcpelauncher_hook / mcpelauncher_preinithook resolve against RedRock’s libmcpelauncher_mod.so.
Play uses this Google account. Confirm it is the one that owns Minecraft, then sign in or switch from here.
Not signed in · tap to sign in
This account does not own Minecraft
